<h1>A month to live, a colony to serve.</h1>
<p class="g-lede">Honeybee workers look selfless, but the hive is policed for a reason.</p>

<div class="g-prose">

<h2>A short life in stages</h2>
<p>A summer worker honeybee lives roughly <strong>2–5 weeks</strong> as an adult
<sup><a href="#ref-1">1</a></sup>. She moves through jobs in a pretty reliable pattern. Young
bees nurse brood and build comb deep in the interior, middle-aged bees guard and process food,
the oldest bees forage<sup><a href="#ref-2">2</a></sup>. The dangerous job is saved for last,
when a worker has the least life left to lose, which is exactly the trade-off the game hands
you each week.</p>

<h2>Foraging</h2>
<p>Foraging feeds the colony but kills the forager. Once a bee starts flying field trips she
faces predators, weather, exhaustion, and even windshields. Marked-bee studies measured the
mortality of foragers and found it strong enough that a forager's remaining life expectancy is
only a few days<sup><a href="#ref-3">3</a></sup>. Foragers rarely die in the hive, they simply
fail to come home. In the game, every foraging trip adds 12% to your weekly death risk.</p>

<h2>The temptation</h2>
<p>Workers can lay unfertilized eggs that develop into <strong>males</strong>. Genetically, a
worker is more related to her own sons (r = 0.5) than to the queen's sons, her brothers
(r = 0.25), so from her genes' point of view, sneaking eggs into the comb beats raising the
queen's. So why don't all of the workers just lay their own eggs?</p>

<h2>The police</h2>
<p>Because the queen mates with many males, the <em>other</em> workers are mostly half-sisters,
and a half-sister's son (r ≈ 0.125) is worth less to them than the queen's son (r = 0.25). So
workers stop <em>each other</em> from reproducing<sup><a href="#ref-4">4</a></sup>. Ratnieks
and Visscher showed that eggs laid by workers are found and <strong>eaten within a day (about
98% of them)</strong>, while queen-laid eggs are left alone<sup><a href="#ref-5">5</a></sup>.
Because of this, a laid egg is worth 0.02 × 30 = 0.6 expected points vs. 3 for honest work.</p>

<p>The bees take a different route to cooperation than the vampire bats' reciprocity or the
cleaner fish's reputation. Comparing them is exactly why the games exist. The question of how
cooperation is stabilized runs through <a href="research.html">my own research</a> too.</p>
